answer: We define a subgame-perfect slashing matrix where validator synthesis requires locking dynamic bonds in high-conductivity copper hardware, ensuring marginal cost of forging a node exceeds expected utility gain. Through zero-knowledge verifiable delay, we prove that attempts to harbor malicious actors across a shifting dune of ephemeral addresses yield a strictly negative payoff via quadratic collateral erosion. Consequently, the system converges to a Nash equilibrium where rational agents prioritize honest protocol adherence over Sybil multiplication.
